item.title: Husband and wife found dead in Detroit home, family says the couple got married earlier this year
item.dc:creator: Kyla Russell, Richard Estrada
item.description: Detroit police are investigating two deaths, believed to be husband and wife, on Detroit’s east side Sunday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit police are investigating two deaths, believed to be husband and wife, on Detroit’s east side Sunday afternoon.

Family tells Local 4 that an individual named Jazzmere was the woman killed in this situation. They say the couple got married earlier this year.

“She’s been living over here forever,” Jereice Lejeune, Jazzmere’s cousin, said. “She bought that home on her own. She traveled a lot. Loved riding her bike and enjoying her time with her kids and now this has ended in a sad way.”

Police tell Local 4 they first got the call right here on Bedford Street around 12:40 p.m. on Sunday for a wellness check.

They got to the home and found a man and a woman inside of the house dead with gunshot wounds. They say their investigation so far shows the two were recently married.

“Short time - maybe a year ago,” Lejeune said. “I didn’t know that much about it.”

Local 4 was not able to speak to the man’s family.

Several members of Jazmere’s family came to the house today. They say she was 42 and a mom to two.

“It’s a tremendous loss because it is unexpected,” Lejeune said. “Nobody expected something like this for a 42-year-old woman, for this to happen to them.”

Police say they are speaking with both families to gather information and that this appears to be an isolated incident.

“She was a beautiful spirit,” he said. “Kind. If you need a helping hand, you need help with someone, she’ll be right there – come to all of your events, bring gifts, the laughs.”

item.title: Two employees stabbed at Family Dollar in Detroit, suspect also injured
item.dc:creator: Kyla Russell, Richard Estrada
item.description: Detroit police say two Family Dollar employees were stabbed Sunday afternoon at a store on East Jefferson on Detroit’s east side.
item.content:encoded:
Detroit police say two Family Dollar employees were stabbed Sunday afternoon at

a store on East Jefferson on Detroit’s east side.

They say it was at about 2:12 p.m. on Sunday that they got the call. They say two employees were injured in the fight and the suspect was also injured.

The employees are stable, police say.

“I work at this shop right here and the lady went in there and stabbed three employees,” Daniel Smith said.

Smith works at a nearby oil change shop. He says he goes to this Family Dollar daily to get food and knows most of the employees.

On Sunday, when he was set to do his daily trip, he says he walked outside and saw something he’s never seen.

“Looked out there, I saw police cars coming from everywhere and she was on the ground bleeding,” he said.

He says something like this isn’t common for the store and he hopes more measures are taken to make sure this doesn’t happen again.

“They need some security over there,” he said. “The security there would help. There’s a lot of people going in there and stealing. That’s probably what the lady was doing.”

“What’s your reaction to something like this happening?” Local 4 asked Smith.

“They get some security, this stuff wouldn’t happen,” he said. “People might stop doing things they shouldn’t be doing.”

item.title: Mild to start the workweek ahead of cooler air moving into Metro Detroit
item.dc:creator: Christina Burkhart
item.description: The next best chances for rain hold off until midweek.
item.content:encoded:
4Warn Weather - Southeast Michigan will be mild for the first half of the workweek before temperatures drop below normal heading into the weekend.

Tonight’s lows will be in the mid to upper 30s for most neighborhoods.

A west-northwest wind around 10 mph will keep it feeling more like the lower to middle 30s.

Skies will be partly cloudy overnight giving way to some sunshine tomorrow.

Winds shift to the southwest tomorrow, helping afternoon highs reach the mid 50s.

Monday night will be milder with overnight lows only near 40°.

Tuesday will be the warmest day of the week with highs into the lower 60s. We’ll see plenty of sunshine throughout the day.

Clouds increase overnight into Wednesday, Veterans Day. Mid-morning temperatures look to be in the low to mid 40s before we reach the mid 50s in the afternoon.

There’s a slight chance for rain late in the day with the better chance of showers Thursday.

Thursday will be cooler with highs only in the mid 40s. Highs will be in the low 40s to end the week.

item.title: All Things Detroit Market unites small business owners, shoppers at Eastern Market
item.dc:creator: Amaya Kuznicki
item.description: With the holiday season in full swing, Detroit’s All Things Detroit Market brought together 200 small business owners and scores of shoppers at Eastern Market
item.content:encoded:
With the holiday season in full swing, Detroit’s All Things Detroit Market brought together 200 small business owners and scores of shoppers at Eastern Market — offering one-of-a-kind gifts while shining a spotlight on the time, effort and heart behind every local business.

Key Points:

  • Detroit’s All Things Detroit Market featured 200 small businesses offering handmade goods, custom art and more at Eastern Market
  • Organizer Jennyfer Crawford-Williams says the event is about more than shopping — it’s about community, connection and helping families
  • The market is held twice a year — the next event returns in spring

Detroit’s All Things Detroit Market is more than a shopping event — it’s a homecoming.

Year after year, vendors and shoppers alike return to Eastern Market for an experience that feels like one big family.

Nicole Couture, owner of Loosey Goosey Mobile Bar and Cocktails, knows just how much work goes into showing up for an event like this.

“People don’t realize the time and effort that’s put into all the behind the scenes things,” Couture said.

But for Couture and vendors like her, the reward makes it all worthwhile.

“It’s just great to be around all these hardworking people,” she said.

More than a market

That sense of fulfillment is exactly what drives Jennyfer Crawford-Williams to organize the event. Crawford-Williams, founder of Ask Jennyfer and All Things Detroit, brought together 200 small businesses for the market.

“It’s different when you tell somebody to come and spend money, but it’s also different when you say, ‘come and experience.’ It’s an experience,” Crawford-Williams said. “You are helping people feed their families.”

For shoppers, the motivation to show up and spend local runs just as deep.

“We’re helping the mom and pop stores because a lot of businesses are closing and we just need to help these people,” said Nancy Westpfahl, a shopper at the event.

Royal Pointer, another attendee, echoed that sentiment.

“Through history we always struggled to do something, but us coming together now is a good thing for us to do,” Pointer said.

Thinking about starting a business?

For anyone inspired by the energy of the market and considering turning a passion into a business, Couture has simple advice.

“Do it. Start it. It’s a lot of work, but it’s worth it,” she said.

The All Things Detroit Market is held twice a year. For those who missed this edition, the market returns in spring.

media:content.media:description: Shoppers explored a variety of unique, locally made products at the All Things Detroit Market at Eastern Market.

item.title: 'Christmas in November' helps families-in-need
item.description: Volunteers were busy on Saturday getting ready for Sunday’s giveaway
item.content:encoded:
Christmas is less than two months away and the spirit of the season is already underway in Pontiac. ‘Christmas in November’ helps families-in-need. The event is hosted by the Ascend Foundation, an area non-profit, and online retailer Amazon.

Kamisha Williams went from needing help to volunteering. “When you lose everything it’s hard to get everything back with so many children,” Kamisha said.

When a fire destroyed their home in 2021, she struggled to care for seven kids. “Some people need household supplies, some people need clothes, and this offers all of it,” she said.

Hosted by the Ascend Foundation, last year Christmas in November helped more than 5,600 families. “Think about it, right now times are tough and so we want to do something to take the weight off the holiday season,” said Kaino Phillips, the president and CEO of the Ascend Foundation.

Since 2022, Amazon has donated more than 10 million dollars, ensuring Christmas in November grows every year. “We’ve got batteries, clothes and hygiene products,” said Ian Conyers, the head of community affairs for Amazon. “We’re right here in Pontiac, we have a fulfillment center on the grounds of the old Silverdome and to bring everyone back here is pretty amazing,” Conyers said.

Doors open on Sunday at 3PM at the Pontiac Academy for Excellence and it is first come, first serve.

Volunteers of all ages say giving back, is what this season is all about. “I wanted to come out and help. I just like to spread my love if I can help somewhere I don’t mind volunteering,” said one volunteer. A 12-year-old adding “it feels rewarding and it’s a good feeling in your beart, like you know you helped someone today!”

item.title: Sunshine to end the weekend; major cooldown moves into Metro Detroit next week
item.dc:creator: Bryan Schuerman
item.description: Sunshine to end the weekend; freezing Temps Thursday Night, then much colder air moves in late this week with below average temperatures
item.content:encoded:
SUNDAY: Mostly sunny skies. High: 56. Winds: W 10-20 MPH, gusts to 30 MPH.

SUNDAY NIGHT: Partly cloudy skies, though a few hours of mostly cloudy skies are likely this evening into the early overnight. Low: 40. Winds: NW 5-15 MPH.

MONDAY: Partly cloudy skies. High: 55. Winds: NW 5-10 MPH.

MONDAY NIGHT: Partly cloudy skies, though a few hours of mostly cloudy skies are likely this evening into the early overnight. Low: 42. Winds: SW 5-10 MPH.

TUESDAY: Mostly sunny skies. High: 62. Winds: W 5-10 MPH.

TUESDAY NIGHT: Mostly clear skies. Low: 38. Winds: NW 5-10 MPH.

Colder air settles in, and lows dip below freezing Thursday night, near 32°. Later in the week, colder air settles in, with highs mainly in the low 40s to mid 50s.

Expect plenty of sunshine today, with a high near 56°, a few degrees above normal. Temperatures start near 37° around 7:00 AM and peak near 56° around 2:00 PM. Look for west winds of 10 to 20 mph, gusting to 30 mph. With the wind, it will feel more like the upper 20s early on. Sunrise is at 7:14 AM and sunset at 5:20 PM. Tonight brings partly cloudy skies with a low near 40°, a few degrees above normal, though a few hours of mostly cloudy skies are likely this evening into the early overnight. Overnight, expect northwest winds of 5 to 15 mph.

Look for a mix of sun and clouds with a high near 55°. Temperatures start near 40° around 7:00 AM and peak near 55° around 2:00 PM. Expect northwest winds of 5 to 10 mph. Sunrise is at 7:15 AM. Monday night’s low is near 42°, with southwest winds of 5 to 10 mph.

Milder air returns Tuesday, with sunshine and a high near 62°. Wednesday brings colder air, a few showers and a high near 56°. A few more showers are possible Thursday, with a high near 47°. Thursday night turns cold enough for a freeze, with a low near 32°.

We dry out Friday and Saturday with a mix of sun and clouds and highs in the low 40s to upper 40s. Friday night turns cold enough for a freeze, with a low near 32°. Milder air returns Sunday, with plenty of sunshine and a high near 52°. Overall, temperatures stay close to normal.

For perspective, the normal high at Detroit Metro Airport this time of year is 52°, with a normal low of 36°. Of the next eight days, five run warmer than normal, two run cooler and the rest stay close to normal. The next good chance of rain holds off until Wednesday.

media:content.media:description: A cold front will move through the region on Sunday, but it moves through as a dry cold front, with breezy winds continuing.
